purpose: Screen two additional San Agustin Table 1 labels against current taxonomic authority and Philippine voucher context.

method.scope: Focused review of Dussumieria acuta and Eleotris fusca, two printed labels in the 2025 San Agustin article Table 1.
method.distinction: A broad country-level range or separately cataloged Philippine museum specimen is context only; it does not identify the San Agustin survey fish or connect it to a named site or reach.
method.evidenceLimit: The survey article provides no voucher accession crosswalk, diagnostic images, meristic data, sequence, station coordinates, or individual reach-to-specimen link. The examined Eleotris fusca paper lists a Philippine voucher under that species but does not include it among the paper's DNA tissue samples.
method.sourceReuse: Only concise attributed findings and direct source links are retained. No specimen image, occurrence export, sequence, taxonomic table, coordinates, or transformed app row was copied. Public-app reuse approval was not assessed or granted.

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk returned an exact accepted species-rank name match. This is a name match only; it does not establish the identity of the San Agustin specimen.
findings.currentAuthority: The Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes online version updated 13 August 2026 treats Dussumieria acuta as valid and gives an Indo-West Pacific range from East Africa, Oman, the Persian Gulf, and Madagascar east to Vietnam and the Philippines, north to Taiwan; habitat is marine. Hata, Lavoué, and Motomura (2025) summarize recent redescription and resurrection of nominal Dussumieria species. Their comparative COI table includes a D. acuta sample from Ha Long Bay, Vietnam, which is a taxonomic study sample and not a San Agustin or Philippine occurrence.
findings.philippineContext: The 2025 study also examines Philippine Dussumieria material assigned to other named congeners, including D. albulina specimens from Palawan and Iloilo/Panay and D. elopsoides material from Manila Bay. This illustrates why a genus-level lookalike or an older label needs a voucher-level diagnostic crosswalk; it does not contradict the Catalog's broad Philippine range for D. acuta and does not identify the survey fish.
findings.disposition: The current specialist Catalog supports broad Philippine range context, so no new range-authority discrepancy or voucher-priority mismatch is added. Keep the San Agustin label regionally plausible but locally unresolved pending the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk; do not turn the Catalog range or separate Philippine congener records into a local occurrence.
findings.priority: routine; request the RSU accession and diagnostic crosswalk before assigning this label to a San Agustin site or reach

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk returned an exact accepted species-rank name match. This does not identify the San Agustin specimen.
findings.currentAuthority: The Catalog of Fishes online version updated 13 August 2026 treats Eleotris fusca as valid, summarizes an Indo-Pacific distribution, and lists freshwater, brackish, and marine habitat. Mennesson and Keith (2017) discuss a cryptic Indian Ocean lineage within the E. fusca group and revalidate E. klunzingerii for that lineage, so historical names and identification context require care.
findings.philippineContext: In its material examined under E. fusca, Mennesson and Keith list MNHN 2015-0375, a 71 mm male from Alegre, Philippines, collected 5 February 2014. The paper's separate DNA tissue-sample table does not include this Philippine voucher; it is published specimen context, not genetic confirmation of that specimen and not evidence from San Agustin.
findings.disposition: The current broad range and separately cataloged Philippine specimen support national context, so no new range-authority discrepancy or voucher-priority mismatch is added. The individual San Agustin fish and any waterbody or reach assignment remain unresolved until its RSU voucher and station crosswalk are available.
findings.priority: routine; request the RSU accession and compare diagnostic characters before assigning this label to a San Agustin site or reach

nextAction: Continue the current-authority and range screen for the remaining 15 of 39 Table 1 labels. Keep six voucher-priority mismatch labels in the verification queue and retain four separate range-authority discrepancies: Tridentiger trigonocephalus, Hypseleotris cyprinoides, Eleotris mauritiana, and Awaous guamensis. Then seek the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk and resolve the paper's station/locality conflicts before considering occurrence rows.

sources.supports: The original 2025 San Agustin article and the verbatim Table 1 species labels; the article remains the source of the local survey labels.
